title: [MVCC performance] Reduce measured public-write allocation hotspots
body:
Parent execution graph: #4871. Coordinator and acceptance owner: `/root`; implementation delegates must be GPT-6.1 Sol. User explicitly authorized parallel ownership of significant allocation sources on 2026-10-15. This is performance-first work: finish a coherent public-path improvement, measure it early, retain focused safety checks throughout, and run exhaustive/current-head qualification before merge.

## Latest public-write comparison — exact pre-sprint and ordinary sources

The merged allocation candidate has now been compared with the exact pre-sprint source and ordinary control using the unchanged public `BenchmarkConditionalTxnBaselineBatchWrite` fixture. [All nine raw samples, source/binary identities, commands and receipts](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/tree/514dab33ef07ab09cacb89efd862043a59f15318/artifacts/4871/20261015-allocation-triad) are published and read back; the coordinator independently recomputed the medians.

| Source | ns/op | operations/s | B/op | allocations/op |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Pre-sprint `28aea01e` | 45,144 | 22,151 | 152,663 | 281 |
| Ordinary `177fb0c8` | 47,476 | 21,063 | 154,839 | 286 |
| Combined `a22078f5` | 21,314 | 46,918 | 31,943 | 127 |

Combined versus pre-sprint: **52.79% less time, 79.08% fewer bytes and 54.80% fewer allocation objects**. Versus ordinary: 55.11%, 79.37% and 55.59% respectively. These are combined measurements; component percentages are not added. Candidate `a22078f5` and merged `5bca87ff` have the same entire Git tree.

Three rotating fixed-1,000-write samples per source, Go1.26.3/Linux111, CPU0/GOMAXPROCS1. The unchanged default-engine fixture seeds 10,000 keys and checkpoints every eight writes with the timer stopped; final partial-group Close is outside timing. Timed groups assert no intervening root publication, and checkpoints assert debt is drained. Source/binary censuses match before and after. All planned samples are retained; no reruns or diagnostic instrumentation. Boundary snapshots showed no competing Go/benchmark/profile process, without claiming continuous host monitoring.

This closes the missing **short** exact-baseline/pre-sprint comparison. Full eight-repeat micro, matched M0/Dgraph sprint targets and native ACK/Q32 acceptance remain open in #4878/#4879. #5130 remains open for finite shared native/ordinary integration evidence; full #4878 acceptance is not a prerequisite for closing #5130. Native construction continues concurrently.

The arena-first workflow is installed and [skills PR #25](https://github.com/snissn/skills/pull/25) is merged as `e8a56cdd`. Its [Go performance skill](https://github.com/snissn/skills/blob/e8a56cddb57d078564f09895b7e0a67fa74f49ea/go-performance-optimization/SKILL.md) requires reuse of suitable maintained arenas/buffers, last-consumer/reset/retention checks, and a documented contract or measured reason for alternatives. An exception does not waive public performance evidence.


Earlier component construction and delivery history follows; pending pre-sprint statements below are superseded by the comparison above.

Source-bound evidence: [direct CPU, mutex/block and Rate=1 allocation profiles](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/ad0ddefac30705fde312e6dc57964c36efd16a17/artifacts/4871/20261015-direct-bottleneck-profiles/report.md), artifact `ad0ddefac30705fde312e6dc57964c36efd16a17`. Baseline ordinary source `177fb0c8db1d19c79d3d975126b4b0b64019568e`, Go1.26.3/Linux111. The denominator is the exact public `db.(*Batch).Write` stack, excluding seed WriteSync and stopped-timer Checkpoint stacks: 464,099,984 allocated bytes. Profile percentages overlap when cumulative; flat rows do not. This diagnostic is not a sprint performance acceptance, and allocator costs substantially predate the sprint.

Keep existing WAL/publication/retirement authorities and persistent value-log ownership. DURABLE acknowledges a dependency-complete stable WAL prefix plus publication without a full checkpoint; RELAXED retains kernel-drained WAL plus publication without fsync. No unsafe aliasing, global scratch pool, duplicate allocator, moved setup work, larger cap, reduced fixture, or weakened Q32/native gates. Native #4878 retains its actual Set/binding/Finish, cursor/projection and materialized-write seams. The paused R1 graph is a source/design supplier, not resumed or accepted by this issue.

Required workflow: enumerate applicable AGENTS; inspect/reuse preserved work before implementing; meaningful test-first public regression with activation evidence, or explicit rationale when an equivalent representation optimization cannot meaningfully fail a behavioral test. Include realistic public caller plus ownership/fallback controls. Before broad suites, run short matched public BatchWrite A/B with identical fixture and environment, separate setup/ACK/maintenance boundaries, B/op, allocs/op, CPU attribution and retained memory if reuse changes lifetime. Use three short paired measurements for a directional decision; do not claim final acceptance from profiles or helper benchmarks. Existing final #4879 eight-repeat micro, M0/Dgraph, durability, native-work, recovery, race, platform, review and required current-head CI gates remain binding. Negative/noisy results trigger a design decision, not an endless optimization loop.

Merge only the coherent integrated packet after predecessor contracts and policy gates pass. Root owns Git/GitHub mutations, graph/PR state and final acceptance. Report exact source/evidence identities, commands, unresolved risks and released generated-data/worktree paths. Preserve unique/dirty/evidence-bearing material; delete only exact released targets after consumers finish.

## Allocation workstream and completion

Prioritize the measured top allocation classes with three distinct owners: (1) canonical allocator topology/page encoding, (2) allocator transaction-private state reuse, (3) zipper merge scratch. Reuse preserved #5103/#5105/#5108 / draft #5123 deliberately, retaining their paused R1 acceptance boundaries. Encoding and private-state owners agree the same canonical representation before changing shared interfaces; no independently optimized legacy topology. They may construct provisionally in parallel, but compose and qualify one allocator implementation. Zipper is independent.

Public Write CPU: allocator preparation 54.92% cumulative; mallocgc 33.68% overlaps it. Public Write allocation flat sources: encodeIndexPage 42.79%, cloneStateNode 11.31%, stateChunk.clone 9.05%, newMergeScratch 7.18%, encodeChunkPage 5.71%. Encoding union 57.23%, state-cloning union 20.35%; do not sum overlapping cumulative percentages.

- [x] All three children have explicit ownership, implementation or evidence-backed disposition, early public cost evidence, and coherent integration.
- [x] Combined candidate measured against this exact baseline and pre-sprint source; report both wins and residual regressions, no double counting component savings.
- [ ] Affected native/ordinary paths consume the same maintained implementation and retain all original gates.
- [x] Accepted code is merged with required review/CI; final sprint performance acceptance remains #4879.

Native GitHub sub-issues and blocking dependencies will be linked after creation. This allocation tracker blocks final #4879 qualification; it does not block ongoing native construction or resume the whole R1 graph.

- #5133 **CLOSED**: independent [PR #5134](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/pull/5134) merged `9029eb4e`; all 50 current-head checks passed and four merged files matched. [Evidence](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/3744b999531fcc4bb76a144a359d2be475dd6bf0/artifacts/4871/20261015-zipper-clone-scratch/README.md): 7.29% fewer B/op, 12 fewer objects, neutral directional latency.
- Native#4878 continuesconcurrently. DelegatesrequestedGPT6.1Sol; serialGo/profilewindows, userauthorizedfour-workerceiling; rootgraph/integration.

Accepted canonicalcompressedstateNode/directchunk/explicitprivatefirstwrite+freeze contracts remain binding; no unrelatedR1credit/manifestimport; wholeR1paused.


## Measured construction and main delivery — 2026-10-15

The allocator changes have a reviewed main candidate, commit `cf93b0b64c3688d59d6e265cf3db52b35e572275`, based on `3f87d74b98e8b1e809d151611be03785f85e2283`. [Source, independent review, commands and raw results](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/5936ecf934248b7956a3030196be0208051b68a9/artifacts/4871/20261015-main-allocator-allocation/README.md) are pushed and verified. All 18 committed blobs match the reviewed and tested source.

Three alternating short public `Batch.Write` pairs on main show **152,734 → 43,074 B/op** (71.80% fewer bytes), **281 → 139 allocations/op**, and median **46,297 → 22,473 ns/op** (21,600 → 44,498 operations/s). Every pair improves; timing remains directional. The unchanged benchmark uses a 10,000-key seed, fixed 1,000 writes, CPU 0, GOMAXPROCS=1 and a stopped-timer checkpoint every eight writes. Separate diagnostic instrumentation confirms private-path activation; timed binaries contain no instrumentation.

Full freelist and focused DB format, fresh creation, readonly, reopen and fallback checks passed. Independent GPT-6.1 Sol review accepted the main projection without actionable findings. Main retains its existing snapshot API and inline append accounting. The pre-alpha allocator format requires `freelist_patricia_v2` and rejects incompatible nonempty older state before relevant filesystem effects.

The [earlier construction packet](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/71d6bbd802bba83e4bad9d3eb87123f2da84e975/artifacts/4871/20261015-allocator-allocation-workstream/README.md) separately isolates mechanisms: named disjoint flat encoding/digest allocation falls 81.18%; the fair historical private-mutation comparison cuts public allocated bytes 19.42% and clone bytes, including mandatory detachment, 66.41%. These have distinct source/denominator bindings; do not add component savings or relabel the original overlapping stack attribution.

**Delivery:** #5131 and #5132 are in [one coherent PR #5135](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/pull/5135), preserving their separate targets and #5132's dependency on #5131. Sole finalizer `/root/allocation_zipper_5133_sol61` owns its current-head CI/review/merge and final changed-file readback. Zipper PR #5134 already merged with all 50 checks passing; #5133 is closed. Final-base integration and the short affected qualification are complete. Allocator PR gates and merge are complete; #5130 remains open for its explicit cross-path/pre-sprint acceptance, retained in #4878/#4879. Original pre-sprint, M0/Dgraph, native ACK/Q32 and final sprint qualification remain open; native implementation continues in parallel.

**Latest repaired candidate (2026-10-15):** [PR #5135](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/pull/5135), head `7702c2a28f9c45266977ec708688717f4e19fd6a`.

| Median | Matched baseline | Repaired allocator + zipper | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| B/op | 141,463 | 31,944 | -77.42% |
| allocations/op | 269 | 127 | -52.79% |
| ns/op | 45,212 | 21,356 | -52.76% |

Three alternating fixed-1,000-write public `Batch.Write` pairs; timing remains directional. Both builds retain merged zipper main `9029eb4e` **and the same new root-lifetime repair**. The baseline restores 17 allocator Go inputs, so the recovery fix cannot explain the measured allocator difference. Full Go/module input census stays unchanged. [Raw pairs, runner/overlay, exact hashes, RED/normal/race and independent review evidence](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/blob/fad5aad24cd72d190e67df2e1475a23ec99adb9d/artifacts/4871/20261015-allocator-repair/README.md) are pushed and read back.

Public SetSync RED exposed premature reuse of a root record still referenced by the surviving recovery slot. The repair retains it through the **actual successor CommitSeq**; format-config consumers, fresh IgnoreFormatConfig and the index-only snapshot fixture are repaired coherently. Four focused normal commands and the focused race pass. Independent GPT-6.1 Sol review accepts all 16 repair blobs; 15 original allocator paths remain unchanged, with renewed review of the other three. No recovery assertions or performance thresholds were weakened.

## Merged delivery and remaining graph acceptance — 2026-10-15

**Delivered:** [PR #5135](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/pull/5135) merged as `5bca87ffe6e1bfba2d693264d2dc82936adc234f` from final head `a22078f59bfe9023787d5147c51c989a4010644d`. All **51** current-head checks passed, including TreeDB, platforms/race and the unchanged M0 gate. Hosted Codex completed clean; CodeRabbit findings were dispositioned and every thread resolved. The finalizer and coordinator independently verified all **31** changed blobs in merged main. #5131 and #5132 are closed; #5133 was already delivered by PR #5134.

[Final CI/review/merge and independent readback evidence](https://github.com/snissn/gomap/tree/c0a1b9459e5b313265a71653ef1e7f415469cdb7/artifacts/4871/20261015-allocator-repair/merged-5bca) is durable. The measured production/public-benchmark inputs at `7702c2a2` are identical to final `a22078f5`; its additional commit changes only the snapshot fixture. The final head's M0 run `38691793798` passed. The earlier `7702` foreground-p99 variance failure is retained; its unchanged-head retry was cancelled by the subsequent push, so no completed retry or unrelated-flake claim is made.

The repaired matched public comparison remains **141,463 → 31,944 B/op**, **269 → 127 allocations/op**, and **45,212 → 21,356 ns/op** over three alternating fixed-1,000-write pairs. Both builds include the same root-lifetime repair and merged zipper; timing is directional. This accepts the scoped component delivery and measured allocation reductions. The original pre-sprint comparison, M0/Dgraph sprint targets and native production ACK/Q32 requirements remain open in #4878/#4879; these short component runs do not satisfy them. The same canonical allocator has been projected into the native owner with focused classifier/pin controls passing, while actual bounded activation and ordinary backintegration remain that owner's responsibility.


## Arena reuse requirement

For remaining material allocation work, inventory and reuse gomap's maintained arenas, batch buffers and scratch by default where their lifetimes fit. The completion packet must identify the chosen mechanism and last consumer, reset/release and retention bounds, or give a source-linked lifetime/API mismatch or measured public-path reason for an alternative. An arena exception does not waive public performance evidence. Apply the [Go performance skill](https://github.com/snissn/skills/blob/e8a56cddb57d078564f09895b7e0a67fa74f49ea/go-performance-optimization/SKILL.md) through the planner/executor workflow.

The read-only audit of candidate `a22078f59bfe9023787d5147c51c989a4010644d` found existing batch arenas, node builder pools and clone-family zipper scratch. Its allocator encoders already expose destination-taking helpers. `CandidatePageWriterV1` explicitly permits retaining page views, and COW nodes/chunks can survive into successor generations and snapshots; resetting their storage at preparation or publication would violate those contracts. Preserve their immutable output ownership rather than forcing batch-lifetime reuse. Source anchors: `TreeDB/freelist/generation_v1_format.go` (writer contract and encoders), `generation_v1_txn.go` (candidate output), `generation_v1_tree.go` (persistent COW), `TreeDB/batch/batch.go`, `TreeDB/node/builder.go`, and `TreeDB/zipper/zipper.go`.

Nonescaping numerical preparation scratch is a possible remaining arena domain. Remove unnecessary expansion/scanning first, then profile the residual path before claiming savings or adding work. This source audit supplies no new measured speedup and does not invalidate the existing measured candidate.
